reason: Abstract explicitly names TYR and OCA2 genes and discusses LRMDA/OCA7 as one of the seven albinism genes. The paper directly studies pathogenic variants in these three genes (all listed as gene_or_topic) causing oculocutaneous albinism, including a digenic TYR/OCA2 case. Directly on-topic.

Title names the K3/K12 keratin pair; K12 is the protein product of KRT12. The paper studies K12 expression during corneal epithelial differentiation in chick and rabbit, directly relevant to KRT12 biology. The abstract is empty but the title is unambiguous.
Abstract explicitly includes 'prcd (PRCD-mutation)' as one of four canine retinal degeneration models studied for miRNA expression changes. PRCD is directly investigated in this paper.

Abstract maps progressive retinal atrophy locus in Finnish lapphund and concludes 'The locus for progressive rod-cone degeneration is known to be close to the GALK1 locus... This suggests that the disease in this breed, as well as in the Swedish lapphund, may correspond to progressive rod-cone degeneration.' PRCD is the gene symbol for progressive rod-cone degeneration; directly relevant.

Title and abstract directly study 'progressive rod-cone degeneration (prcd)' in Miniature Poodle dogs, the same gene as PRCD. Abstract discusses PRCD inheritance patterns and draws comparison to retinitis pigmentosa.

Review of canine inherited retinal degenerations notes linkage studies have identified genetic markers for a retinal degeneration 'found in at least six different breeds.' PRCD was precisely the multi-breed disease under linkage investigation at this period. As a review covering the entire field, it covers PRCD research. Relevant to PRCD.

Abstract explicitly states 'The Papillon dog is another dog breed affected by progressive rod-cone degeneration, with similarities to the canine retinal disease given the gene symbol prcd.' PRCD is named by its gene symbol. Directly relevant.

Title describes evaluation of phosducin as a candidate gene for canine generalized progressive retinal atrophies. Abstract is empty. Phosducin was investigated during the PRCD gene discovery effort as one of several photoreceptor-expressed candidates. Relevant to PRCD research context even if phosducin was ultimately ruled out.

Title describes characteristics of the human ocular surface epithelium, the tissue where KRT12 is the hallmark corneal keratin. KRT12 expression and function in the ocular surface epithelium would be expected content in such a review. No abstract available but the subject matter is directly tied to KRT12.

Title directly studies keratin expression by corneal and limbal stem cells during development. KRT12 is the primary keratin expressed in corneal epithelium and is a defining marker of corneal stem cell differentiation. Directly relevant to KRT12. Abstract empty but title is unambiguous.

Meesmann corneal dystrophy is caused specifically by mutations in KRT3 or KRT12. A paper on managing Meesmann dystrophy is directly relevant to KRT12. Abstract empty but the disease-gene link is unambiguous.

Abstract describes butterfly-shaped pattern dystrophy, one of the best-characterized phenotypes caused by PRPH2 mutations. Search keywords include both 'PRPH2' and 'pattern-dystrophy'. Although the abstract does not name PRPH2 explicitly, butterfly-shaped pattern dystrophy is prototypically a PRPH2-associated disorder and the paper is directly relevant to PRPH2.

Peripherin/RDS is an alias for PRPH2. Abstract explicitly studies a large deletion in the peripherin/RDS gene causing butterfly-shaped macular dystrophy, performing linkage analysis and molecular characterization of the PRPH2 mutation. Directly relevant.
Peripherin/RDS is PRPH2. Abstract studies a 4-bp insertion at codon 140 of the peripherin/RDS gene causing dominantly inherited pattern dystrophy. Directly relevant to PRPH2.
Peripherin/RDS is PRPH2. Title describes a splice site mutation in the peripherin/RDS gene causing pattern dystrophy. Directly relevant to PRPH2. Abstract is empty but title is unambiguous.

HMX1 mutations cause oculoauricular syndrome, which includes both microtia and structural eye defects (the reason HMX1 is in the ophthalmogenetics library). A review of the genetic causes of microtia would cover HMX1 as a causative gene with known ophthalmic co-phenotype. Relevant to HMX1.

Abstract is entirely about non-coding cis-regulatory HK1 variants causing congenital hyperinsulinism via loss of beta-cell repression. The paper focuses solely on pancreatic beta-cell biology and insulin secretion; no retinal or ophthalmic content is mentioned. HK1 is in this ophthalmogenetics library for its retinal dystrophy role, not its metabolic role. A paper focused exclusively on the hyperinsulinism phenotype of HK1 is off-topic for an ophthalmogenetics library.

Title describes a novel NK-related mouse homeobox gene expressed in nervous structures during embryonic development. HMX1 is an NK-related homeobox gene (H6 family, also called NKX5-3), and the search keywords include both HMX1 and NKX5-3. This paper likely characterizes HMX1 or a direct homolog; expression in neural structures during embryogenesis is consistent with HMX1's known role in sensory organ development. Abstract is empty but title and gene aliases match strongly.
